paper.title_en: Role of matter-electromagnetic coupling in constructing dark energy stellar configurations in f(R, T) gravity
paper.abstract_en: In the context of f(R, T) gravity, this work introduces two novel compact spherical solutions for dark energy objects. A system of modified field equations is derived from a cornerstone of a static, charged inner spacetime. These assumptions characterize a geometric structure made up of two different matter distributions. Within the framework of the fluid-geometry coupling, we investigate the coupling of dark energy with ordinary matter by introducing two different equations of state. Two independent solutions are formulated by closing the field equations with two distinct spacetime models, namely the Finch-Skea and Tolman IV metrics. The values of the constants are determined in each case by matching the interior and exterior metrics at the boundary of the stellar object. Subsequently, we define the essential constraints that guarantee stellar models to be physically feasible. To evaluate the proposed models, we utilize observational data from SAX J1808.4–3658 and Her X-1. The analysis also includes evaluating two specific charge and several model parametric choices. Our analysis confirms that, for particular parametric choices, both stellar configurations are physically stable.
